reverse_expectations.model: 10-year DCF on economic owner cash; FY27 revenue midpoint anchors year 0; starting owner-cash margin equals TTM company FCF less SBC diagnostic (~-3.6%); margin ramps linearly; net liquid cash added at end.
reverse_expectations.interpretation: At the reference price, the market roughly requires ~19% annual revenue growth for a decade while economic owner-cash margin expands from slightly negative to ~25%. This is feasible only for a durable category winner; it is not a low-expectation price.

bear.thesis: Core cyber-recovery demand persists but growth normalizes quickly, RAC fails to become material, pricing/competition limit margin, and SBC remains economically heavy.

base.thesis: Rubrik remains a top cyber-resilience platform, continues land-and-expand, gains some identity/AI-control revenue, and gradually converts SBC-heavy FCF into owner cash.

bull.thesis: Rubrik becomes a control-and-recovery layer for enterprise data, identity and autonomous agents; RAC creates a second growth curve and scale drives strong owner-cash margins.

subjective_probability_example.note: Subjective scenario weighting for asymmetry discussion only; not a target price.

permanent_loss_case.description: AI-agent control fails to monetize; legacy data protection becomes commoditized or bundled; NRR and new ARR slow sharply; SBC dilution stays high; channel/supply disruption hurts execution; valuation compresses to mature software levels. Solvency is not the central loss mechanism.

sensitivity_note: Terminal value is material. The model intentionally treats SBC as an economic compensation cost rather than ignoring dilution. If SBC falls substantially while growth remains above 20%, value rises materially; using company-defined FCF without an SBC adjustment would raise value but may overstate owner economics.
